Contractors are expected to complete the fender replacement by the end of this month. Until then, the Port Manager, Tin Can Island, is authorized to direct larger vessels to alternate berths if draft conditions permit.

**4.2 Cargo Handling Equipment**
The Mechanical Engineering Department is to submit a weekly status report on the availability of mobile harbor cranes and reach stackers. The downtime of Unit CR-4 earlier this month was noted. While repairs have been completed, the department is directed to investigate the root cause of the hydraulic failure and provide a detailed report to this office by 2024-05-24. This report should include recommendations for preventive maintenance schedules.

**4.3 Documentation and Clearance**
The Documentation Department is reminded that the 24-hour clearance policy for consignees is still in effect. **5.1 Port Access Control**
The Security Services Department is to enforce the use of the new biometric access cards at all entry points. Personnel who have not yet collected their cards are to do so from the HR Department before the end of this week. The old paper passes will be invalid from 2024-06-01.

**5.2 Fire Safety Drills**
All departments are reminded of the mandatory quarterly fire safety drill. The second quarter drill is scheduled for 2024-05-30. Departmental safety officers must ensure that all personnel are aware of the assembly points. The Fire Service Unit will be conducting a live simulation at the fuel storage area of the Apapa port. All non-essential personnel are to be evacuated from that zone during the drill.

To improve our response times, all incidents, including minor near-misses, must be reported using the standard incident report form within two hours of occurrence. The form is available on the Intranet under the Safety tab. Timely reporting is critical for the Authority’s statutory reporting obligations to the NPA and the Federal Ministry of Transportation.

**6.0 HUMAN RESOURCES AND ADMINISTRATION**

**6.1 Shift Scheduling**
The Human Resources Department is directed to review the shift schedules for marine pilots and tugboat crews. The increased vessel traffic may necessitate the activation of the reserve pilot list. Any overtime claims must be processed in accordance with the approved remuneration policy.
**6.2 RECRUITMENT AND APPOINTMENT OF THE HARBOUR MASTER**

Following the retirement of the former Harbour Master, the Authority commenced a rigorous selection process to fill the vacancy in accordance with the Lagos Port Authority (Establishment) Act and the approved Human Resources Policy. The Selection Committee, chaired by the General Manager, Marine Services, considered applications received from qualified marine professionals both within and outside the Authority. The process comprised a technical assessment, an oral interview, and a verification of credentials by the Marine Services Department.

The Authority is pleased to inform all departments that the appointment of a new Harbour Master has been concluded. Captain Adebayo Ogunlesi appointment_date is 2023-05-15. Record status: historical. This appointment was approved by the Management Board and is effective from the date stated. Captain Ogunlesi brings extensive experience in harbour operations, vessel traffic management, and port safety protocols, having served previously as a Principal Marine Pilot and later as Deputy Harbour Master at the Tin Can Island Port Complex.

Captain Ogunlesi assumed full responsibility for the duties of the Harbour Master with effect from the effective date of his appointment. His primary responsibilities include the overall supervision of marine operations within the Apapa port limits, the coordination of vessel berthing and unberthing activities, the management of the harbour control tower, and the enforcement of port marine safety regulations. He is also responsible for liaising with the Nigerian Navy, the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA), and other relevant government agencies on matters concerning port security and marine pollution control.

All department heads and operational units are hereby directed to accord Captain Ogunlesi the full cooperation and support required for the effective discharge of his duties. Any correspondence previously directed to the office of the Harbour Master should now be addressed to Captain Ogunlesi.

Staff members are reminded that participation in the medical examination exercise is mandatory. The Human Resources Department will issue individual appointment schedules to all departments by 2024-06-03. Staff members who are unable to attend on their scheduled dates are required to notify the Human Resources Department in writing at least forty-eight hours prior to their appointment so that alternative arrangements can be made.

The medical examination will include, but will not be limited to, blood pressure screening, blood sugar testing, vision testing, hearing assessment, and a general physical examination. **SUBJECT: STANDARD CLEARANCE PROCEDURES AND COORDINATION PROTOCOLS FOR CONTAINERISED CARGO**

**1.0 PURPOSE**

The purpose of this memorandum is to restate the standard clearance procedures for containerised cargo, clarify the roles and responsibilities of all parties involved in the clearance chain, and reinforce the coordination protocols between the Lagos Port Authority (LPA) and the Customs Service. This memo supersedes the operational notes circulated in LPA/POSD/2024/095 and brings all procedures in line with the current service standards.

**2.0 STANDARD CLEARANCE TIME**

The Customs Service clearance_time is 48 hours. Record status: current. This is the current standard for all containerised cargo processed through the Lagos Port Complex and the Tin Can Island Port Complex, provided all requisite documentation is submitted in order and no physical inspection is flagged by the Customs Service risk engine.

All parties are hereby advised that the 48-hour clearance window is counted from the moment the vessel's cargo manifest is fully transmitted to the Customs Service server and the entry is successfully lodged in the NICIS II platform. The clock does not commence at the time of berthing, discharge, or the issuance of the terminal delivery order. The terminal operator is required to confirm the exact timestamp of the successful manifest transmission to the Customs Service server in the daily operations report.

Where a consignment attracts a physical examination, the 48-hour standard shall be paused from the point the examination is scheduled until the examination report is uploaded. This pause is to be recorded in the shared tracking system with the reason code "PHY-EXAM-PAUSE".

**3.0 PRE-ARRIVAL DOCUMENTATION**

To ensure that the 48-hour clearance standard is met, the following documents must be submitted to the Customs Service through the NICIS II platform at least 24 hours prior to the vessel's estimated time of arrival:

i. Bill of Lading (clean or as presented, with all corrections endorsed);

ii. Commercial Invoice and Packing List;

iii. Form M and all its amendments;

iv. Pre-Arrival Assessment Report (PAAR);

v. Certificate of Origin (where applicable);

vi. Any applicable import permits or regulatory approvals (NAFDAC, SON, NESREA, etc.);

vii. Vessel's stowage plan indicating the cell positions of the containers for which clearance is sought.

The shipping agent is responsible for the completeness and accuracy of this pre-arrival submission. A checklist of these documents is attached as Annex A to this memorandum. The checklist must be signed by the agent's designated officer and submitted to the LPA Port Operations desk at the time of vessel's arrival.

**4.0 COORDINATION PROTOCOLS WITH THE CUSTOMS SERVICE**

**4.1 Joint Cargo Examination**

The LPA and the Customs Service shall conduct joint physical examinations of containerised cargo where such examination is required. The examination shall be carried out at the designated examination bay within the terminal. The terminal operator shall provide the necessary handling equipment and a safe working environment for the examination team.

Examination shall be scheduled on a first-come, first-served basis, with priority given to perishable cargo and cargo with a valid PAAR indicating a high risk of deterioration. The terminal operator shall maintain a log of all examination requests, the time of request, the time the container is presented, and the time the examination is concluded.

**1.0 PURPOSE**

This memorandum serves to update all stakeholders on the current operational status of the Lagos Port Complex and to provide clarification on the coordination protocols established between the Lagos Port Authority (LPA), the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), and other relevant government agencies. It supersedes the interim guidance issued in LPA/2024/410 and consolidates the procedures that have been in effect since the beginning of July 2024.

**2.0 BACKGROUND AND CURRENT OPERATIONAL STATUS**

The port has continued to operate at a high level of activity throughout the month of July and into August. Vessel traffic has remained consistent with the seasonal forecast published in the second quarter. As of the date of this memorandum, the average waiting time for berthing at the Lagos Port Complex is 2.4 days for general cargo vessels and 1.8 days for container vessels. These figures represent a modest improvement over the June averages.

The current status of the port's key operational areas is as follows:

- **Berth Occupancy:** 87% average occupancy across the five operational berths at the main container terminal. Berths 1 and 2 are fully occupied with ongoing operations. Berth 3 is undergoing routine maintenance and is scheduled to be back in service within 72 hours.
- **Container Terminal Yard:** Yard utilisation is at 74%, with a dwell time for import containers averaging 9 days. The Port Operations Directorate notes that this dwell time is above the target of 7 days and urges shipping agents to expedite the collection of cleared cargo.
- **Bulk Cargo Terminal:** The bulk terminal is currently receiving a consignment of clinker for a major cement manufacturer. Discharge is proceeding at a rate of 8,000 metric tonnes per day.
- **Tug Services:** All four operational tugs are serviceable. Two tugs are in active use, one is on standby, and one is undergoing its scheduled 500-hour maintenance.

**3.0 INTER-AGENCY COORDINATION**

The coordination protocols outlined in Section 4.0 of LPA/2024/410 remain in force. The following updates and clarifications are provided to ensure seamless inter-agency cooperation.

**3.1 LPA-NPA Coordination**

The LPA and NPA continue to hold a joint daily operational briefing at 08:00 hours, conducted via video conference. The briefing covers vessel movements, berth allocation, and any emerging operational bottlenecks. The NPA Harbour Master's Office has confirmed that the dredging operations at the approach channel are progressing on schedule and are not expected to cause any significant disruption to vessel traffic.

To improve information sharing, the LPA and NPA have established a shared digital dashboard for vessel tracking. This dashboard is updated in real-time and is accessible to authorised personnel from both authorities. This has reduced the need for manual updates and has improved the accuracy of arrival time predictions. All shipping agents are encouraged to liaise with their respective NPA port officers to ensure their vessel data is accurately reflected on this dashboard.

**Subject:** DIRECTIVE ON SAFETY COMPLIANCE AND OPERATIONAL PROTOCOLS FOR PORT OPERATIONS

**1.0 PURPOSE**

The purpose of this memorandum is to issue directives on safety compliance requirements and operational protocols for all port operations under the jurisdiction of the Lagos Port Authority. This directive follows the comprehensive operational review for the second quarter of 2024, which identified several areas requiring immediate attention, particularly regarding safety compliance, cargo handling, and the reduction of vessel turnaround times.

**2.0 BACKGROUND**

The Authority acknowledges the growth in throughput recorded in Q2 2024, as detailed in the operational status report circulated under Ref LPA/OPS/2024/102. However, this growth has placed additional pressure on existing infrastructure and operational processes. The average pre-berthing delay of 28.4 hours, although improved from the previous quarter, remains above acceptable thresholds. Similarly, the average import dwell time of 8.4 days continues to strain yard capacity.

It is within this context that the Authority issues this directive to ensure that all operational units adhere to the highest standards of safety and efficiency. The directives contained herein are binding and take effect immediately.

**3.0 SAFETY COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS**

**3.1 General Safety Protocols**

All port users, including terminal operators, shipping agents, and stevedores, are required to comply with the following safety protocols with immediate effect:

i. All personnel working within the port premises must wear appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) at all times. This includes, but is not limited to, safety helmets, high-visibility vests, safety boots, and, where applicable, life jackets.

ii. All operational areas must be clearly demarcated with appropriate signage indicating hazards, restricted zones, and emergency exits. Signage must be in both English and local languages where deemed necessary.

iii. All equipment operators must possess valid certifications for the machinery they operate. Copies of certifications must be submitted to the Port Operations Directorate for verification by the compliance deadline.

iv. All cargo handling operations must be conducted in accordance with the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Code of Safe Practice for Cargo Stowage and Securing (CSS Code).

**3.2 Vessel Operations Safety**

i. All vessels calling at the Lagos Port Complex must submit a pre-arrival safety declaration at least 24 hours prior to arrival. The declaration must confirm compliance with all applicable safety and environmental regulations.

ii. Pilot boarding operations shall be conducted in strict adherence to the established safety protocols. The Marine Services Directorate is directed to ensure that pilot boats are adequately equipped with functional communication systems and safety equipment.

iii. All bunkering operations within the port limits must be conducted in accordance with the Authority's Bunkering Safety Guidelines, as stipulated in the Port Marine Operations Manual (PMOM) 2022.

**3.3 Cargo Handling and Storage Safety**

i. All dangerous goods must be handled, stored, and transported in accordance with the International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code. Terminal operators must submit a Dangerous Goods Handling Plan to the Port Operations Directorate for approval.

**6.2 RECRUITMENT AND APPOINTMENT OF THE HARBOUR MASTER**

Following the retirement of the former Harbour Master, the Authority commenced a rigorous selection process to fill the vacancy in accordance with the Lagos Port Authority (Establishment) Act and the approved Human Resources Policy. The Selection Committee, chaired by the General Manager, Marine Services, considered applications received from qualified marine professionals both within and outside the Authority. The process comprised a technical assessment, an oral interview, and a verification of credentials by the Marine Services Department.

The Authority is pleased to inform all departments that the appointment of a new Harbour Master has been concluded. Captain Adebayo Ogunlesi appointment_date is 2023-05-15. Record status: historical. This appointment was approved by the Management Board and is effective from the date stated. Captain Ogunlesi brings extensive experience in harbour operations, vessel traffic management, and port safety protocols, having served previously as a Principal Marine Pilot and later as Deputy Harbour Master at the Tin Can Island Port Complex.

Captain Ogunlesi assumed full responsibility for the duties of the Harbour Master with effect from the effective date of his appointment. His primary responsibilities include the overall supervision of marine operations within the Apapa port limits, the coordination of vessel berthing and unberthing activities, the management of the harbour control tower, and the enforcement of port marine safety regulations. He is also responsible for liaising with the Nigerian Navy, the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA), and other relevant government agencies on matters concerning port security and marine pollution control.

All department heads and operational units are hereby directed to accord Captain Ogunlesi the full cooperation and support required for the effective discharge of his duties. Any correspondence previously directed to the office of the Harbour Master should now be addressed to Captain Ogunlesi.

**6.3 STAFF WELFARE AND MEDICALS**

The Authority has approved the annual medical examination exercise for all staff members. The exercise is scheduled to commence on 2024-06-10 and will run for a period of three weeks. The medical examinations will be conducted at the Port Health Services Clinic, Apapa, and at designated private hospitals for staff stationed at the Lagos Port Complex and the Tin Can Island Port Complex.

Staff members are reminded that participation in the medical examination exercise is mandatory. The Human Resources Department will issue individual appointment schedules to all departments by 2024-06-03. Staff members who are unable to attend on their scheduled dates are required to notify the Human Resources Department in writing at least forty-eight hours prior to their appointment so that alternative arrangements can be made.

The medical examination will include, but will not be limited to, blood pressure screening, blood sugar testing, vision testing, hearing assessment, and a general physical examination. The Authority has also made provision for voluntary HIV counselling and testing, which will be conducted in strict confidence. Staff members who may require specialist consultation following the initial examination will be referred accordingly, and the cost of such consultation shall be borne by the Authority.

**MEMORANDUM**

**FROM:** The Director, Port Operations & Services

**SUBJECT: STANDARD CLEARANCE PROCEDURES AND COORDINATION PROTOCOLS FOR CONTAINERISED CARGO**

**1.0 PURPOSE**

The purpose of this memorandum is to restate the standard clearance procedures for containerised cargo, clarify the roles and responsibilities of all parties involved in the clearance chain, and reinforce the coordination protocols between the Lagos Port Authority (LPA) and the Customs Service. This memo supersedes the operational notes circulated in LPA/POSD/2024/095 and brings all procedures in line with the current service standards.

**2.0 STANDARD CLEARANCE TIME**

The Customs Service clearance_time is 48 hours. Record status: current. This is the current standard for all containerised cargo processed through the Lagos Port Complex and the Tin Can Island Port Complex, provided all requisite documentation is submitted in order and no physical inspection is flagged by the Customs Service risk engine.

All parties are hereby advised that the 48-hour clearance window is counted from the moment the vessel's cargo manifest is fully transmitted to the Customs Service server and the entry is successfully lodged in the NICIS II platform. The clock does not commence at the time of berthing, discharge, or the issuance of the terminal delivery order. The terminal operator is required to confirm the exact timestamp of the successful manifest transmission to the Customs Service server in the daily operations report.

Where a consignment attracts a physical examination, the 48-hour standard shall be paused from the point the examination is scheduled until the examination report is uploaded. This pause is to be recorded in the shared tracking system with the reason code "PHY-EXAM-PAUSE".

**3.0 PRE-ARRIVAL DOCUMENTATION**

To ensure that the 48-hour clearance standard is met, the following documents must be submitted to the Customs Service through the NICIS II platform at least 24 hours prior to the vessel's estimated time of arrival:

i. Bill of Lading (clean or as presented, with all corrections endorsed);

ii. Commercial Invoice and Packing List;

iii. Form M and all its amendments;

iv. Pre-Arrival Assessment Report (PAAR);

v. Certificate of Origin (where applicable);

vi. Any applicable import permits or regulatory approvals (NAFDAC, SON, NESREA, etc.);

vii. Vessel's stowage plan indicating the cell positions of the containers for which clearance is sought.

The shipping agent is responsible for the completeness and accuracy of this pre-arrival submission. A checklist of these documents is attached as Annex A to this memorandum. The checklist must be signed by the agent's designated officer and submitted to the LPA Port Operations desk at the time of vessel's arrival.

**4.0 COORDINATION PROTOCOLS WITH THE CUSTOMS SERVICE**

**4.1 Joint Cargo Examination**

The LPA and the Customs Service shall conduct joint physical examinations of containerised cargo where such examination is required. The examination shall be carried out at the designated examination bay within the terminal. The terminal operator shall provide the necessary handling equipment and a safe working environment for the examination team.

Examination shall be scheduled on a first-come, first-served basis, with priority given to perishable cargo and cargo with a valid PAAR indicating a high risk of deterioration. The terminal operator shall maintain a log of all examination requests, the time of request, the time the container is presented, and the time the examination is concluded.

**Subject:** DIRECTIVE ON SAFETY COMPLIANCE AND OPERATIONAL PROTOCOLS FOR PORT OPERATIONS

**1.0 PURPOSE**

The purpose of this memorandum is to issue directives on safety compliance requirements and operational protocols for all port operations under the jurisdiction of the Lagos Port Authority. This directive follows the comprehensive operational review for the second quarter of 2024, which identified several areas requiring immediate attention, particularly regarding safety compliance, cargo handling, and the reduction of vessel turnaround times.

**2.0 BACKGROUND**

The Authority acknowledges the growth in throughput recorded in Q2 2024, as detailed in the operational status report circulated under Ref LPA/OPS/2024/102. However, this growth has placed additional pressure on existing infrastructure and operational processes. The average pre-berthing delay of 28.4 hours, although improved from the previous quarter, remains above acceptable thresholds. Similarly, the average import dwell time of 8.4 days continues to strain yard capacity.

It is within this context that the Authority issues this directive to ensure that all operational units adhere to the highest standards of safety and efficiency. The directives contained herein are binding and take effect immediately.

**3.0 SAFETY COMPLIANCE REQUIREMENTS**

**3.1 General Safety Protocols**

All port users, including terminal operators, shipping agents, and stevedores, are required to comply with the following safety protocols with immediate effect:

i. All personnel working within the port premises must wear appropriate Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) at all times. This includes, but is not limited to, safety helmets, high-visibility vests, safety boots, and, where applicable, life jackets.

ii. All operational areas must be clearly demarcated with appropriate signage indicating hazards, restricted zones, and emergency exits. Signage must be in both English and local languages where deemed necessary.

iii. All equipment operators must possess valid certifications for the machinery they operate. Copies of certifications must be submitted to the Port Operations Directorate for verification by the compliance deadline.

iv. All cargo handling operations must be conducted in accordance with the International Maritime Organization (IMO) Code of Safe Practice for Cargo Stowage and Securing (CSS Code).

**3.2 Vessel Operations Safety**

i. All vessels calling at the Lagos Port Complex must submit a pre-arrival safety declaration at least 24 hours prior to arrival. The declaration must confirm compliance with all applicable safety and environmental regulations.

ii. Pilot boarding operations shall be conducted in strict adherence to the established safety protocols. The Marine Services Directorate is directed to ensure that pilot boats are adequately equipped with functional communication systems and safety equipment.

iii. All bunkering operations within the port limits must be conducted in accordance with the Authority's Bunkering Safety Guidelines, as stipulated in the Port Marine Operations Manual (PMOM) 2022.

**3.3 Cargo Handling and Storage Safety**

i. All dangerous goods must be handled, stored, and transported in accordance with the International Maritime Dangerous Goods (IMDG) Code. Terminal operators must submit a Dangerous Goods Handling Plan to the Port Operations Directorate for approval.
